# All-level endpoint extrusion and residual-mass height coupling

This note proves necessary geometric inequalities for the actual planar
all-zero-B three-cap regime. It also records exact scalar tests of the
individual inequalities, then shows how whole-A and cross-direction
information exclude those tests. Neither diagnostic menu is an actual
convex-fiber counterexample. No general OC closure is asserted.

Use the canonical triangle

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1),
    T={x:v_i.x<=1},          |T|=9/2.

Let A,K,B be actual full planar fibers at -1,0,1 with
(A+B)/2 subset K and B subset T. Suppose 0 is interior to K and
all three H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z} attain the source's genuine raw depth
Q, every A cut is proper, and every B capture has zero area. Genuine
criticality forces h_B(v_i)=1: otherwise moving the B threshold
slightly toward B decreases the proper A capture while leaving B
empty and the middle trace fixed.

Write the A cap areas in increasing order as u<=v<=w, and let v_l
be the normal associated to w. Set

    q=Q-w, h=h_A(v_l), H=h+1,
    delta=a-u-v,        a=|A|, k=|K|, b=|B|.

The full residual-height conclusions below are used only under the
hypothetical bad-source assumptions

    b<=a+k,        Q<=(2/9)(a+k+b).                 (1)

## 1. The actual missing intersection controls the entire height

The two ordinary cap-cover profiles are

    a<=w+v+u/4,
    k<=(9/4)Q-u-v-w/4.

They follow from the positive-part cap-cover inequality at the minimum
cap volume; its complete proof is in the companion aligned-simplex
note. Combining the middle profile with (1) and b<=a+k gives
u+v+w/4<=a. Thus

    delta>=w/4>0.                                  (2)

The intersection of the two strict missed A regions has area at least
a-u-v=delta. Every such point has v_l-coordinate greater than 2,
so h>2 and H>3. In particular the original largest cap

    D=A intersect {v_l.x>=-1}

has area w and contains at least delta area above level 2.
Choose a point p_- on its minimum level v_l.x=-1. Such a point
exists because the original cut is proper. The homothety

    p_-+(3/H)(D-p_-)

lies in D and below level 2. Its area is (3/H)^2 w. Since the area
of D above level 2 is at least delta, it follows that

    delta <= w[1-(3/H)^2],
    H >= 3 sqrt[w/(w-delta)].                       (3)

This also proves delta<w. Consequently, putting

    r=delta/w,       s=sqrt(1-r),

one has

    1/4<=r<1,       0<s<=sqrt(3)/2,
    H>=3/s>=2sqrt(3).                              (4)

The estimate retains the actual residual fraction r, rather than only
the universal quarter lower bound in (2).

## 2. Every actual B section gives an extrusion inequality

For -2<=t<=1 define the normalized section length

    ell(t)=H_1(B intersect {v_l.x=t})/|v_l|,

with ell(t)=0 if the section is empty. Coarea gives

    b=int_(-2)^1 ell(t) dt,
    0<=ell(t)<=t+2.                                (5)

The upper bound is the exact section length of T in this normalization.
Let A_t=A intersect {v_l.x>=-t}. Contract D toward a point attaining
its maximum h by the factor

    (h+t)/(h+1)=(H-1+t)/H.

This factor lies in (0,1] because H>3 and -2<=t<=1. The contracted
copy lies in A_t, hence

    |A_t|>=w[(H-1+t)/H]^2.                         (6)

If the B section at t is nonempty, its Minkowski average with A_t
lies in the original K cap. The exact segment-extrusion formula gives

    4q >= |A_t|+ell(t)(H-1+t).

The section-normalized factor is exact: segment length is
|v_l|ell(t), and A_t's perpendicular width is (H-1+t)/|v_l|.
For an empty section, ell(t)=0 and the same lower bound on 4q
follows by pairing A_t with a B support point at level 1. Its midpoint
is still in the K cap because 1-t>=0. Thus for every t in [-2,1],

    4q >= w[(H-1+t)/H]^2+ell(t)(H-1+t).             (7)

No sum over B fibers has replaced this actual one-fiber section identity.
In particular,

    ell(t)<=min{t+2,
           4q/(H-1+t)-w(H-1+t)/H^2}.              (8)

Genuine fixed-normal tilt equalization gives w<=2q: at a tilt where
the endpoint captured areas are both t_0, actual Brunn--Minkowski
bounds t_0<=q, and criticality gives w<=2t_0. The t_0=0 case is
trivial. Thus the second term in (8) is positive throughout the range.

## 3. Exact integral envelope

Put A_0=H-3>0 and change variables x=H-1+t. Equation (8) gives

    b<=int_(A_0)^H min{x-A_0, 4q/x-wx/H^2} dx.      (9)

The first term increases and the second decreases. If 4q>=3H+w,
the right side is simply |T|=9/2. Otherwise let

    x_0=[A_0+sqrt(A_0^2+16q(1+w/H^2))]
                         /[2(1+w/H^2)].

Then A_0<x_0<H, and the integral is exactly

    b <= 2q-(A_0/2)(x_0-A_0)-w/2
                                  +4q log(H/x_0). (10)

Indeed the crossing equation is
(1+w/H^2)x_0^2-A_0 x_0=4q. Integrating x-A_0 below x_0 and
4q/x-wx/H^2 above x_0, then substituting that equation, gives (10).
The first endpoint inequality uses w<=2q, which makes the second
term in (9) positive at A_0; the second is exactly 4q<3H+w.

A weaker bound that uses only H>3 is also explicit. Put z=(t+2)/3.
Then (H-1+t)/H>=z and H-1+t>=3z, so

    ell(3z-2)<=min{3z,(4q-wz^2)/(3z)}

for 0<z<=1. When 4q<9+w, integration at
z_0^2=4q/(9+w) gives

    b<=2q[1+log((9+w)/(4q))]-w/2.                  (11)

Under (1), the original cap profiles imply Q<=2+w/3, hence
4q<=8-(8/3)w<9+w. Thus the nontrivial branch in (11) applies to
every hypothetical bad configuration considered here.

## 4. Concavity supplies a complementary bound retaining delta/w

Let the projection of B on the v_l coordinate be [1-L,1], where
0<L<=3. Its upper endpoint is 1 by the actual support contact.
Convexity of B implies that ell is concave on this interval: the
Minkowski convex combination of any two interval sections lies in the
intermediate section, and interval lengths add linearly. Thus Jensen,
or integration of the symmetric midpoint inequality, gives

    b<=L ell(1-L/2)
      <=L[4q/(H-L/2)-w(H-L/2)/H^2].               (12)

The last expression increases with L for 0<L<=3. Its derivative is

    4qH/(H-L/2)^2-w/H+wL/H^2
        >=(4q-w)/H>0,

using q>=w/2 and w>0. Consequently

    b<=12q/(H-3/2)-3w(H-3/2)/H^2.                 (13)

This upper expression decreases with H>3. Its derivative is

    -12q/(H-3/2)^2+3w(H-3)/H^3
       <(-12q+3w)/H^2<0.

Substituting H>=3/s from (4) into (13) gives the exact coupled bound

    b <= [8s/(2-s)]q-[s(2-s)/2]w.                 (14)

This need not dominate (10) pointwise in all parameters; both are
valid necessary inequalities.

The bad original cap profile also gives

    Q<=(4/9)(b+delta-w/4),
    b>=(9/4)q+(5/2-r)w
      =(9/4)q+(3/2+s^2)w.                         (15)

Combining (14)--(15) proves

    (41s-18)q >=2(2-s)(s^2+2s+3)w.                (16)

Since w,q>0 and 0<s<1, its right side is positive. Therefore

    s>18/41,
    delta/w <1357/1681.                            (17)

For example the formal profile a=1/10,u=v=1/160,w=19/200 has
r=35/38, so s^2=3/38<(18/41)^2. It cannot satisfy these necessary
conditions of an actual bad critical configuration. Its exclusion is
an exact certificate, not a numerical test.

## 5. A diagnostic menu for the D-only inequalities

Here is an exact scalar menu that passes both bulk bounds, the D-only
height-mass bound, and the previously used scalar constraints:

    u=v=1/40,       w=1/20,      q=1/10,
    Q=3/20,         a=3/40,      k=43/160,
    b=1/3,          delta=1/40,  H=17/4.

It is not asserted to arise from actual compatible convex fibers.
It only certifies that the displayed scalar restrictions alone cannot
close the remaining geometric problem.

Here r=1/2, s=1/sqrt(2), and H^2=289/16>18=9/(1-r), so (3)
holds strictly. The A profile has upper bound13/160>a=12/160, and
the K profile has upper bound44/160>k=43/160. The largest mass is
b and b<a+k=11/32, so every fiber is nonheavy. The ordinary centroid
comparisons all pass, since

    Q-(4/9)b=1/540>0.

Tilt equalization passes because w<2q. The whole-body Brunn--Minkowski
restriction also passes: a+b=49/120 and sqrt(ab)=1/sqrt(40)<1/6,
so (sqrt(a)+sqrt(b))^2/4<89/480<k=129/480.

Nevertheless M=65/96 and

    (2/9)M-Q=1/2160>0.

The concavity upper bound (13) at H=17/4 is

    24/55-33/1445 >1/3=b.

For the integral envelope (9), A_0=5/4. On the subinterval
x in [8/5,4], the linear capacity x-A_0 is at least7/20, while
the second capacity is at most4q/x<=1/4. Thus the minimum there
is the second capacity. Since H>4, this interval lies in the
integration range. The complete integral is at least

    (2/5)log(5/2)-672/36125
      >(2/5)log(5/2)-7/375.

The convergent positive series for log[(1+z)/(1-z)], with z=3/7,
gives

    log(5/2)>2[3/7+(3/7)^3/3]=312/343>22/25.

Consequently the last integral lower bound exceeds 1/3; an explicit
rational margin is

    (2/5)(312/343)-7/375-1/3=508/42875>0.

Thus the exact integral bound and the complementary concavity bound
both allow this menu. The weaker envelope (11) allows it as well.
Sections8--9 add further actual geometry and exclude this menu. This
calculation only distinguishes what the preceding inequalities supply.

## 6. Joint cap-root interpolation sharpens the retained A term

There is a stronger bound than the maximizer homothety in (6), because
the same A body retains at least delta area at level 2. For
s_0=(t+2)/3 in [0,1], ordinary Brunn--Minkowski applied to the actual
caps at levels -1 and 2 gives

    |A intersect {v_l.x>=-t}|^(1/2)
       >=s_0 sqrt(w)+(1-s_0)sqrt(delta).

Indeed the corresponding Minkowski convex combination is inside the
cap at level s_0(-1)+(1-s_0)2=-t. Therefore (7) strengthens to

    4q >=w[s_0+(1-s_0)sqrt(r)]^2
                              +ell(t)(H-1+t).      (18)

Using concavity of ell at the projection midpoint as in Section 4,
where s_0=1-L/6, gives

    b<=L/(H-L/2)
             [4q-w(1-(L/6)(1-sqrt(r)))^2].          (19)

The right side increases with L in (0,3]: the first factor increases,
the bracket is positive and increases because q>=w/2 and
0<=L(1-sqrt(r))/6<=1/2. It decreases as H increases. Consequently
H>=3/s, with s=sqrt(1-r), yields

    b <= [2s/(2-s)]
                  [4q-(w/4)(1+sqrt(r))^2].         (20)

This retains both pieces of actual A information, its far tail and
its total height. It is stronger than the separate homothety term
used in (14). It still does not exclude the menu in Section 5.

## 7. The menu survives exact one-direction concave-density geometry

A stronger certificate is possible than checking only the formulas
above. For the Section 5 values H=17/4,w=1/20, take the affine
probability density on normalized cap height x in [0,1]

    f(x)=(1+238x)/120.

It is nonnegative and concave, integrates to one, and is realizable
as the normalized parallel-section density of a genuine planar
trapezoid D of height H and area w. For example, on physical height
z in [0,H] give D a centered interval section of length
(w/H)f(z/H). Its two affine boundary graphs define a convex trapezoid.

The exact upper-tail probability is

    R(x)=1-x/120-(119/120)x^2.

It satisfies

    R(3/H)=R(12/17)=1/2=r,
    R((3/2)/H)=R(6/17)=297/340.

Thus the full tail mass constraint and the exact one-direction
concave section geometry can hold simultaneously at this menu. The
corresponding midpoint-Jensen upper bound for b is

    [3/(H-3/2)][4q-w R((3/2)/H)]
       =(12/11)[2/5-(1/20)(297/340)]
       =7269/18700>1/3.

Even the all-level integral envelope obtained from this exact marginal
retention function remains above b. Since 0<=R<=1, its second capacity
on the x-variable range of (9) is at least

    (4q-w)/x=(7/20)/x.

For x in [3/2,H], the first capacity x-A_0=x-5/4 is also at least
(7/20)/x: at x=3/2 the product x(x-5/4)=3/8 exceeds7/20, and
that product increases on this interval. Therefore the integral of
the minimum of these two exact capacities is at least

    (7/20)log(H/(3/2))=(7/20)log(17/6).

The positive logarithm series, now with parameter11/23, gives
log(17/6)>22/23. Hence this lower bound is strictly greater than

    77/230>1/3,

with rational margin1/690. In particular even the exact one-direction
section-density constraints cannot eliminate this scalar menu.

Only D and its single normal marginal are realized in this paragraph.
No assertion is made that the other two A caps, a common B, a common
compatible K, and the mixed criticality conditions can be realized
simultaneously. Whole-A extendibility is also required; Section8 already
excludes this particular marginal witness before cross-direction
compatibility is tested.

## 8. Whole-A concavity strengthens the height and excludes the first menu

The D-only restrictions above do not enforce extension across the original
cut into the residual A mass a-w. Here is the stronger necessary height.
For 0<=t<=H put

    F(t)=|A intersect {v_l.x+1<=t}|^(1/2).

This function is concave: the Minkowski interpolation of two lower caps
lies in the lower cap at the interpolated level, so ordinary planar
Brunn--Minkowski applies. The proper original cut ensures F(0)=sqrt(a-w)
with a-w>0. Also F(H)=sqrt(a), while the actual upper tail at level3
has mass at least delta. Thus F(3)<=sqrt(a-delta). Concavity between
levels0 andH gives

    H >= 3[ sqrt(a)-sqrt(a-w) ]
                 /[ sqrt(a-delta)-sqrt(a-w) ].      (21)

The denominator is positive because delta<w. If a stronger valid lower
bound tau_0<=|A intersect {v_l.x>=2}| is available, the same proof
replaces delta in (21) by tau_0.

The first menu in Section5 is excluded by (21). Its a/w=3/2 and
r=1/2 give

    H>=3(sqrt(3)-1)/(sqrt(2)-1)>5.

The strict inequality follows from 3sqrt(3)+2>5sqrt(2): squaring
reduces it to sqrt(3)>19/12. Even the weak midpoint-retention bound
w/4, which follows from cap-root interpolation, then gives

    b <(6/7)(4q-w/4)=93/280<1/3.

Consequently that menu is an obstruction only to the earlier D-only
inequalities. It is not an obstruction after whole-A concavity is added.
The affine D density in Section7 cannot be extended to the required
whole A mass while keeping its prescribed height.

## 9. A shifted ordinary cover gives a further cross-direction charge

There is a stronger actual tail lower bound than delta. Let

    tau=|A intersect {v_l.x>=2}|.

The two original smaller caps and this shifted largest-normal cap
cover the entire plane: their three normal vectors sum to zero and
the three thresholds -1,-1,2 sum to zero. Apply the ordinary positive-
part cover inequality at the minimum of their areas. Since u<=v,

    a<=u+v+tau-(3/4)min(u,tau),
    tau>=delta+(3/4)min(u,tau).                    (22)

Under the bad assumptions, delta>=w/4>=u/4. If tau<u, (22) would
give tau>=4delta>=u, a contradiction. Hence

    tau >= delta+(3/4)u
         =a-v-u/4 =: delta_*.                      (23)

This is a quantitative overlap/cross-capture charge for the same A
body in the other two continuous directions. It is valid without any
affine section-density hypothesis. Properness gives u>0, so delta_*
strictly exceeds delta. Every height or retained-volume inequality in
this note may therefore use delta_* in place of delta when its proof
requires only a lower bound on the tail at level2. In particular (21)
becomes

    H >= 3[ sqrt(a)-sqrt(a-w) ]
                /[ sqrt(a-delta_*)-sqrt(a-w) ].      (24)

Here delta_*<w in every actual configuration: the original proper A
cut ensures a positive portion of D lies below level2, whereas its
upper tail is at least delta_*. Thus the denominator is positive.

For another precise illustration, consider the scalar values

    q=1/10, w=1/100, Q=11/100,
    a=1/99, delta=1/275, u=v=8/2475,
    k=119/500, b=247/1000, H=27/7.

A complete one-direction cone would realize the a,w,delta,H values:
its lower-CDF square root grows linearly from0 at level-3/7 to1
at level27/7, taking the normalized values1/10 and4/5 at levels0
and3. These scalar values pass the earlier whole-A height bound with
delta, and they give (2/9)(a+k+b)-Q=1/44550>0.

Nevertheless they cannot realize the other two stated A cap areas.
Equation (23) requires

    tau>=1/275+(3/4)(8/2475)=1/165,

whereas the proposed whole-A cone has tau=1/275. This is an exact
cross-direction contradiction. No geometric counterexample to OC is
provided by either diagnostic menu in this note, and the strengthened
route is not declared blocked on their basis.
